... | inj₂ ¬x  = record
    { sigᵈ      = 𝑆∅
    ; algᵈ      = 𝟏
    ; finiteᵈ   = 𝟏-FiniteAlgebra
    ; finsigᵈ   = 𝑆∅-FiniteSignature
    ; con-isoᵈ  = trivial-ConIsoᵈ-transport
                    {𝑆₁ = Representableᵈ.sigᵈ r} {𝑆₂ = 𝑆∅}
                    {𝑨 = Representableᵈ.algᵈ r} {𝑩 = 𝟏} {𝑳 = 𝑳}
                    (empty→ConTrivialᵈ {𝑨 = Representableᵈ.algᵈ r} ¬x)
                    (𝟏-ConTrivialᵈ {𝑆 = 𝑆∅})
                    (Representableᵈ.con-isoᵈ r)
    } , tt

docs.title: A machine-checked representation: Con(coset action of TransitiveGroup[9, 4] on 9 cosets of H (order 2)) ≅ 2x2 (four-element Boolean lattice)
docs.text:
This is the FLRP.Certificates.Group.TG9x4TwoByTwo module of the Agda Universal Algebra Library.

This module was emitted by scripts/python/flrp/emit_agda.py from scripts/python/flrp/inputs/tg9x4_two_by_two.json. Do not edit it by hand; rerun the emitter instead.

The four-element Boolean lattice 2×2 as the upper interval [H, G] with G = TransitiveGroup(9,4) ≅ C3×S3 and H a point stabilizer (index 9), from the SmallLatticeReps manuscript Figure 10. Found by the issue #487 GAP subgroup-interval engine; this module is the direct-certificate route (coset action → claim → checker).

It re-verifies, end-to-end through the WP-6 certificate pipeline (#457), the claim that the congruence lattice of the algebra "coset action of TransitiveGroup[9, 4] on 9 cosets of H (order 2)" — carrier size 9, unary operations g0, g1, g2 — is isomorphic to the lattice "2x2 (four-element Boolean lattice)" (4 elements). The engine's output below (normal-form parent vectors, Freese traces, and pointer tables) is certificate data only: the search-free checkers of Setoid.Congruences.Certificates re-verify all of it during type-checking, and the FLRP.Certificates assembly turns the checked certificate into the headline theorems — a Representableᵈ witness for the target lattice and a FiniteCongruencesᵈ instance for the algebra. Nothing is believed on the engine's authority: a wrong table or trace would make a decidable check compute to no and break compilation.

{-# OPTIONS --cubical-compatible --exact-split --safe #-}

module FLRP.Certificates.Group.TG9x4TwoByTwo where

-- Imports from Agda and the Agda Standard Library -----------------------------
open import Data.Fin.Base       using ( Fin )
open import Data.Fin.Patterns   using ( 0F ; 1F ; 2F ; 3F ; 4F ; 5F ; 6F ; 7F ; 8F )
open import Data.List.Base      using ( [] ; _∷_ )
open import Data.Vec.Base       using ( Vec ; [] ; _∷_ )
open import Level               using ( 0ℓ )

-- Imports from the Agda Universal Algebra Library -----------------------------
open import Classical.Signatures.Unary   using ( Sig-Unary )
open import Classical.Structures.Unary   using ( tablesToUnaryAlgebra
                                               ; tablesToUnaryAlgebra-FiniteAlgebra
                                               ; Sig-Unary-Fin-FiniteSignature )
open import FLRP.Certificates            using ( MeetMatches ; meetMatches?
                                               ; certRepresentableᵈ )
open import FLRP.Problem                 using ( FiniteLattice ; toLattice )
open import FLRP.Representable           using ( Representableᵈ )
open import Overture.Cayley              using ( Table ; ⟦_⟧ ; from-yes )
open import Overture.Operations.Properties
                                         using ( Associative? ; Commutative?
                                               ; Idempotent? ; Absorbsˡ? ; Absorbsʳ? )
open import Setoid.Algebras.Basic        using ( Algebra )
open import Setoid.Algebras.Finite       using ( FiniteAlgebra )
open import Setoid.Congruences.Certificates.Schema
                                         using ( ParentVec ; Trace ; LatticeCert
                                               ; mkLatticeCert ; mkMerge
                                               ; seed ; translate )
open import Setoid.Congruences.Certificates.Congruence
                                         using ( module CertCheck )
open import Setoid.Congruences.Certificates.Lattice
                                         using ( module LatticeCheck )
open import Setoid.Congruences.Finite.Decidable
                                         using ( FiniteCongruencesᵈ )
open import Setoid.Signatures.Finite     using ( FiniteSignature )

docs.title: The algebra, from its operation tables
docs.text:
Row f of opTables is the value table of the f-th unary operation; Classical.Structures.Unary turns the table into the algebra and its finiteness witnesses.

opTables : Vec (Vec (Fin 9) 9) 3
opTables = (1F ∷ 3F ∷ 4F ∷ 0F ∷ 6F ∷ 7F ∷ 2F ∷ 8F ∷ 5F ∷ [])
         ∷ (2F ∷ 4F ∷ 5F ∷ 6F ∷ 7F ∷ 0F ∷ 8F ∷ 1F ∷ 3F ∷ [])
         ∷ (1F ∷ 0F ∷ 4F ∷ 3F ∷ 2F ∷ 7F ∷ 6F ∷ 5F ∷ 8F ∷ [])
         ∷ []

𝑨 : Algebra {𝑆 = Sig-Unary (Fin 3)} 0ℓ 0ℓ
𝑨 = tablesToUnaryAlgebra 9 3 opTables

𝑭 : FiniteAlgebra 𝑨
𝑭 = tablesToUnaryAlgebra-FiniteAlgebra 9 3 opTables

𝑺 : FiniteSignature (Sig-Unary (Fin 3))
𝑺 = Sig-Unary-Fin-FiniteSignature 3

docs.title: The target lattice, from its Cayley tables
docs.text:
The claimed congruence lattice "2x2 (four-element Boolean lattice)", presented exactly as the worked lattice examples are (Examples.Classical.Lattices.L7): meet and join tables, every law discharged by decision over the finite carrier.

∧-table ∨-table : Table 4
∧-table = (0F ∷ 0F ∷ 0F ∷ 0F ∷ [])
        ∷ (0F ∷ 1F ∷ 0F ∷ 1F ∷ [])
        ∷ (0F ∷ 0F ∷ 2F ∷ 2F ∷ [])
        ∷ (0F ∷ 1F ∷ 2F ∷ 3F ∷ [])
        ∷ []

∨-table = (0F ∷ 1F ∷ 2F ∷ 3F ∷ [])
        ∷ (1F ∷ 1F ∷ 3F ∷ 3F ∷ [])
        ∷ (2F ∷ 3F ∷ 2F ∷ 3F ∷ [])
        ∷ (3F ∷ 3F ∷ 3F ∷ 3F ∷ [])
        ∷ []

open FiniteLattice

𝑳 : FiniteLattice
𝑳 .size     = 3
𝑳 ._∧_      = ⟦ ∧-table ⟧
𝑳 ._∨_      = ⟦ ∨-table ⟧
𝑳 .∧-assoc  = from-yes (Associative? ⟦ ∧-table ⟧)
𝑳 .∧-comm   = from-yes (Commutative? ⟦ ∧-table ⟧)
𝑳 .∧-idem   = from-yes (Idempotent? ⟦ ∧-table ⟧)
𝑳 .∨-assoc  = from-yes (Associative? ⟦ ∨-table ⟧)
𝑳 .∨-comm   = from-yes (Commutative? ⟦ ∨-table ⟧)
𝑳 .∨-idem   = from-yes (Idempotent? ⟦ ∨-table ⟧)
𝑳 .absorbˡ  = from-yes (Absorbsˡ? ⟦ ∧-table ⟧ ⟦ ∨-table ⟧)
𝑳 .absorbʳ  = from-yes (Absorbsʳ? ⟦ ∧-table ⟧ ⟦ ∨-table ⟧)

docs.title: The certificate
docs.text:
The engine's whole-lattice certificate (design note § 4): the congruence list as normal-form parent vectors, indexed by the lattice's carrier; the principal-congruence pointer table with one Freese trace per carrier pair; and the join traces, seeded by forest edges. The meet and join tables are the target's own tables, which is what MeetMatches pins.

open CertCheck 𝑭 𝑺 using ( arOf )

cert : LatticeCert 9 3 arOf 4
cert = mkLatticeCert partsᵛ 0F prinᵛ prinTrᵛ ∧-table ∨-table joinTrᵛ
  where
  partsᵛ : Vec (ParentVec 9) 4
  partsᵛ = (0F ∷ 1F ∷ 2F ∷ 3F ∷ 4F ∷ 5F ∷ 6F ∷ 7F ∷ 8F ∷ [])
         ∷ (0F ∷ 0F ∷ 2F ∷ 0F ∷ 2F ∷ 5F ∷ 2F ∷ 5F ∷ 5F ∷ [])
         ∷ (0F ∷ 1F ∷ 0F ∷ 3F ∷ 1F ∷ 0F ∷ 3F ∷ 1F ∷ 3F ∷ [])
         ∷ (0F ∷ 0F ∷ 0F ∷ 0F ∷ 0F ∷ 0F ∷ 0F ∷ 0F ∷ 0F ∷ [])
         ∷ []

  prinᵛ : Vec (Vec (Fin 4) 9) 9
  prinᵛ = (0F ∷ 1F ∷ 2F ∷ 1F ∷ 3F ∷ 2F ∷ 3F ∷ 3F ∷ 3F ∷ [])
        ∷ (1F ∷ 0F ∷ 3F ∷ 1F ∷ 2F ∷ 3F ∷ 3F ∷ 2F ∷ 3F ∷ [])
        ∷ (2F ∷ 3F ∷ 0F ∷ 3F ∷ 1F ∷ 2F ∷ 1F ∷ 3F ∷ 3F ∷ [])
        ∷ (1F ∷ 1F ∷ 3F ∷ 0F ∷ 3F ∷ 3F ∷ 2F ∷ 3F ∷ 2F ∷ [])
        ∷ (3F ∷ 2F ∷ 1F ∷ 3F ∷ 0F ∷ 3F ∷ 1F ∷ 2F ∷ 3F ∷ [])
        ∷ (2F ∷ 3F ∷ 2F ∷ 3F ∷ 3F ∷ 0F ∷ 3F ∷ 1F ∷ 1F ∷ [])
        ∷ (3F ∷ 3F ∷ 1F ∷ 2F ∷ 1F ∷ 3F ∷ 0F ∷ 3F ∷ 2F ∷ [])
        ∷ (3F ∷ 2F ∷ 3F ∷ 3F ∷ 2F ∷ 1F ∷ 3F ∷ 0F ∷ 1F ∷ [])

docs.title: The verification
docs.text:
One decision for the whole certificate, one for the meet-table match; both compute to yes — that computation is the re-verification of every engine claim above.

open LatticeCheck 𝑭 𝑺

certOK : LatticeCertOK cert
certOK = from-yes (latticeCertOK? cert)

certMeet : MeetMatches 𝑭 𝑺 𝑳 cert
certMeet = from-yes (meetMatches? 𝑭 𝑺 𝑳 cert)

docs.title: The headline theorems
docs.text:
The target lattice is decidably representable, witnessed by this algebra; and the certificate's congruence list is a complete Layer-D enumeration of the algebra's decidable congruences.

TG9x4TwoByTwo-Representableᵈ : Representableᵈ (toLattice 𝑳)
TG9x4TwoByTwo-Representableᵈ = certRepresentableᵈ 𝑭 𝑺 𝑳 cert certOK certMeet

TG9x4TwoByTwo-FiniteCongruencesᵈ : FiniteCongruencesᵈ 𝑨
TG9x4TwoByTwo-FiniteCongruencesᵈ = certFiniteCongruencesᵈ cert certOK

docs.title: A machine-checked representation: Con(the Klein four-group acting on itself) ≅ M3

This module was emitted by scripts/python/flrp/emit_agda.py from scripts/python/flrp/inputs/v4_regular_m3.json. Do not edit it by hand; rerun the emitter instead.

It re-verifies, end-to-end through the WP-6 certificate pipeline (#457), the claim that the congruence lattice of the algebra "the Klein four-group acting on itself" — carrier size 4, unary operations e, a, b, ab — is isomorphic to the lattice "M3" (5 elements). The engine's output below (normal-form parent vectors, Freese traces, and pointer tables) is certificate data only: the search-free checkers of Setoid.Congruences.Certificates re-verify all of it during type-checking, and the FLRP.Certificates assembly turns the checked certificate into the headline theorems — a Representableᵈ witness for the target lattice and a FiniteCongruencesᵈ instance for the algebra. This module was emitted by scripts/python/flrp/emit_agda.py from scripts/python/flrp/inputs/slr/slr01.json. Do not edit it by hand; rerun the emitter instead.

B1/L1 in the numbering of the DeMeo–Freese–Jipsen manuscript Representing Finite Lattices as Congruence Lattices of Finite Algebras (§ 6 of the 2016-06-10 draft, docs/papers/fin-lat-rep/SmallLatticeReps.tex). The dictionary between the manuscript's lattice numbering and this library's names is docs/notes/flrp-slr-naming.md.

It re-verifies, end-to-end through the WP-6 certificate pipeline (#457), the claim that the congruence lattice of the algebra "B1" — carrier size 4, unary operations f, g — is isomorphic to the lattice "manuscript L1 (N5)" (5 elements). This module was emitted by scripts/python/flrp/emit_agda.py from scripts/python/flrp/inputs/slr/slr02.json. Do not edit it by hand; rerun the emitter instead.

B2/L2 in the numbering of the DeMeo–Freese–Jipsen manuscript Representing Finite Lattices as Congruence Lattices of Finite Algebras (§ 6 of the 2016-06-10 draft, docs/papers/fin-lat-rep/SmallLatticeReps.tex). The dictionary between the manuscript's lattice numbering and this library's names is docs/notes/flrp-slr-naming.md.

It re-verifies, end-to-end through the WP-6 certificate pipeline (#457), the claim that the congruence lattice of the algebra "B2" — carrier size 3, unary operations f — is isomorphic to the lattice "manuscript L2 (M3)" (5 elements). The engine's output below (normal-form parent vectors, Freese traces, and pointer tables) is certificate data only: the search-free checkers of Setoid.Congruences.Certificates re-verify all of it during type-checking, and the FLRP.Certificates assembly turns the checked certificate into the headline theorems — a Representableᵈ witness for the target lattice and a FiniteCongruencesᵈ instance for the algebra. Nothing is believed on the engine's authority: a wrong table or trace would make a decidable check compute to no and break compilation.

{-# OPTIONS --cubical-compatible --exact-split --safe #-}

module FLRP.Certificates.SmallLatticeReps.SLR02 where

-- Imports from Agda and the Agda Standard Library -----------------------------
open import Data.Fin.Base       using ( Fin )
open import Data.Fin.Patterns   using ( 0F ; 1F ; 2F ; 3F ; 4F )
open import Data.List.Base      using ( [] ; _∷_ )
open import Data.Vec.Base       using ( Vec ; [] ; _∷_ )
open import Level               using ( 0ℓ )

-- Imports from the Agda Universal Algebra Library -----------------------------
open import Classical.Signatures.Unary   using ( Sig-Unary )
open import Classical.Structures.Unary   using ( tablesToUnaryAlgebra
                                               ; tablesToUnaryAlgebra-FiniteAlgebra
                                               ; Sig-Unary-Fin-FiniteSignature )
open import FLRP.Certificates            using ( MeetMatches ; meetMatches?
                                               ; certRepresentableᵈ )
open import FLRP.Problem                 using ( FiniteLattice ; toLattice )
open import FLRP.Representable           using ( Representableᵈ )
open import Overture.Cayley              using ( Table ; ⟦_⟧ ; from-yes )
open import Overture.Operations.Properties
                                         using ( Associative? ; Commutative?
                                               ; Idempotent? ; Absorbsˡ? ; Absorbsʳ? )
open import Setoid.Algebras.Basic        using ( Algebra )
open import Setoid.Algebras.Finite       using ( FiniteAlgebra )
open import Setoid.Congruences.Certificates.Schema
                                         using ( ParentVec ; Trace ; LatticeCert
                                               ; mkLatticeCert ; mkMerge
                                               ; seed )
open import Setoid.Congruences.Certificates.Congruence
                                         using ( module CertCheck )
open import Setoid.Congruences.Certificates.Lattice
                                         using ( module LatticeCheck )
open import Setoid.Congruences.Finite.Decidable
                                         using ( FiniteCongruencesᵈ )
open import Setoid.Signatures.Finite     using ( FiniteSignature )

docs.title: The algebra, from its operation tables
docs.text:
Row f of opTables is the value table of the f-th unary operation; Classical.Structures.Unary turns the table into the algebra and its finiteness witnesses.

opTables : Vec (Vec (Fin 3) 3) 1
opTables = (0F ∷ 1F ∷ 2F ∷ [])
         ∷ []

𝑨 : Algebra {𝑆 = Sig-Unary (Fin 1)} 0ℓ 0ℓ
𝑨 = tablesToUnaryAlgebra 3 1 opTables

𝑭 : FiniteAlgebra 𝑨
𝑭 = tablesToUnaryAlgebra-FiniteAlgebra 3 1 opTables

𝑺 : FiniteSignature (Sig-Unary (Fin 1))
𝑺 = Sig-Unary-Fin-FiniteSignature 1

docs.title: The target lattice, from its Cayley tables
docs.text:
The claimed congruence lattice "manuscript L2 (M3)", presented exactly as the worked lattice examples are (Examples.Classical.Lattices.L7): meet and join tables, every law discharged by decision over the finite carrier.

∧-table ∨-table : Table 5
∧-table = (0F ∷ 0F ∷ 0F ∷ 0F ∷ 0F ∷ [])
        ∷ (0F ∷ 1F ∷ 0F ∷ 0F ∷ 1F ∷ [])
        ∷ (0F ∷ 0F ∷ 2F ∷ 0F ∷ 2F ∷ [])
        ∷ (0F ∷ 0F ∷ 0F ∷ 3F ∷ 3F ∷ [])
        ∷ (0F ∷ 1F ∷ 2F ∷ 3F ∷ 4F ∷ [])
        ∷ []

∨-table = (0F ∷ 1F ∷ 2F ∷ 3F ∷ 4F ∷ [])
        ∷ (1F ∷ 1F ∷ 4F ∷ 4F ∷ 4F ∷ [])
        ∷ (2F ∷ 4F ∷ 2F ∷ 4F ∷ 4F ∷ [])
        ∷ (3F ∷ 4F ∷ 4F ∷ 3F ∷ 4F ∷ [])
        ∷ (4F ∷ 4F ∷ 4F ∷ 4F ∷ 4F ∷ [])
        ∷ []

open FiniteLattice

𝑳 : FiniteLattice
𝑳 .size     = 4
𝑳 ._∧_      = ⟦ ∧-table ⟧
𝑳 ._∨_      = ⟦ ∨-table ⟧
𝑳 .∧-assoc  = from-yes (Associative? ⟦ ∧-table ⟧)
𝑳 .∧-comm   = from-yes (Commutative? ⟦ ∧-table ⟧)
𝑳 .∧-idem   = from-yes (Idempotent? ⟦ ∧-table ⟧)
𝑳 .∨-assoc  = from-yes (Associative? ⟦ ∨-table ⟧)
𝑳 .∨-comm   = from-yes (Commutative? ⟦ ∨-table ⟧)
𝑳 .∨-idem   = from-yes (Idempotent? ⟦ ∨-table ⟧)
𝑳 .absorbˡ  = from-yes (Absorbsˡ? ⟦ ∧-table ⟧ ⟦ ∨-table ⟧)
𝑳 .absorbʳ  = from-yes (Absorbsʳ? ⟦ ∧-table ⟧ ⟦ ∨-table ⟧)

docs.title: The certificate
docs.text:
The engine's whole-lattice certificate (design note § 4): the congruence list as normal-form parent vectors, indexed by the lattice's carrier; the principal-congruence pointer table with one Freese trace per carrier pair; and the join traces, seeded by forest edges. The meet and join tables are the target's own tables, which is what MeetMatches pins.

open CertCheck 𝑭 𝑺 using ( arOf )

cert : LatticeCert 3 1 arOf 5
cert = mkLatticeCert partsᵛ 0F prinᵛ prinTrᵛ ∧-table ∨-table joinTrᵛ
  where
  partsᵛ : Vec (ParentVec 3) 5
  partsᵛ = (0F ∷ 1F ∷ 2F ∷ [])
         ∷ (0F ∷ 0F ∷ 2F ∷ [])
         ∷ (0F ∷ 1F ∷ 0F ∷ [])
         ∷ (0F ∷ 1F ∷ 1F ∷ [])
         ∷ (0F ∷ 0F ∷ 0F ∷ [])
         ∷ []

  prinᵛ : Vec (Vec (Fin 5) 3) 3
  prinᵛ = (0F ∷ 1F ∷ 2F ∷ [])
        ∷ (1F ∷ 0F ∷ 3F ∷ [])
        ∷ (2F ∷ 3F ∷ 0F ∷ [])
        ∷ []

  prinTrᵛ : Vec (Vec (Trace 3 1 arOf) 3) 3
  prinTrᵛ = ( []
            ∷ (mkMerge 0F 1F (seed 0) ∷ [])
            ∷ (mkMerge 0F 2F (seed 0) ∷ [])
            ∷ [] )
          ∷ ( (mkMerge 1F 0F (seed 0) ∷ [])
            ∷ []
            ∷ (mkMerge 1F 2F (seed 0) ∷ [])
            ∷ [] )
          ∷ ( (mkMerge 2F 0F (seed 0) ∷ [])
            ∷ (mkMerge 2F 1F (seed 0) ∷ [])
            ∷ []
            ∷ [] )
          ∷ []

  joinTrᵛ : Vec (Vec (Trace 3 1 arOf) 5) 5
  joinTrᵛ = ( []
            ∷ (mkMerge 1F 0F (seed 0) ∷ [])
            ∷ (mkMerge 2F 0F (seed 0) ∷ [])
            ∷ (mkMerge 2F 1F (seed 0) ∷ [])
            ∷ ( mkMerge 1F 0F (seed 0)
              ∷ mkMerge 2F 0F (seed 1)
              ∷ [] )
            ∷ [] )
          ∷ ( (mkMerge 1F 0F (seed 0) ∷ [])
            ∷ (mkMerge 1F 0F (seed 0) ∷ [])
            ∷ ( mkMerge 1F 0F (seed 0)
              ∷ mkMerge 2F 0F (seed 1)
              ∷ [] )
            ∷ ( mkMerge 1F 0F (seed 0)
              ∷ mkMerge 2F 1F (seed 1)
              ∷ [] )
            ∷ ( mkMerge 1F 0F (seed 0)
              ∷ mkMerge 2F 0F (seed 2)
              ∷ [] )
            ∷ [] )
          ∷ ( (mkMerge 2F 0F (seed 0) ∷ [])
            ∷ ( mkMerge 2F 0F (seed 0)
              ∷ mkMerge 1F 0F (seed 1)
              ∷ [] )
            ∷ (mkMerge 2F 0F (seed 0) ∷ [])
            ∷ ( mkMerge 2F 0F (seed 0)
              ∷ mkMerge 2F 1F (seed 1)
              ∷ [] )
            ∷ ( mkMerge 2F 0F (seed 0)
              ∷ mkMerge 1F 0F (seed 1)
              ∷ [] )
            ∷ [] )
          ∷ ( (mkMerge 2F 1F (seed 0) ∷ [])
            ∷ ( mkMerge 2F 1F (seed 0)
              ∷ mkMerge 1F 0F (seed 1)
              ∷ [] )
            ∷ ( mkMerge 2F 1F (seed 0)
              ∷ mkMerge 2F 0F (seed 1)
              ∷ [] )
            ∷ (mkMerge 2F 1F (seed 0) ∷ [])
            ∷ ( mkMerge 2F 1F (seed 0)
              ∷ mkMerge 1F 0F (seed 1)
              ∷ [] )
            ∷ [] )
          ∷ ( ( mkMerge 1F 0F (seed 0)
              ∷ mkMerge 2F 0F (seed 1)
              ∷ [] )
            ∷ ( mkMerge 1F 0F (seed 0)
              ∷ mkMerge 2F 0F (seed 1)
              ∷ [] )
            ∷ ( mkMerge 1F 0F (seed 0)
              ∷ mkMerge 2F 0F (seed 1)
              ∷ [] )
            ∷ ( mkMerge 1F 0F (seed 0)
              ∷ mkMerge 2F 0F (seed 1)
              ∷ [] )
            ∷ ( mkMerge 1F 0F (seed 0)
              ∷ mkMerge 2F 0F (seed 1)
              ∷ [] )
            ∷ [] )
          ∷ []

docs.title: The verification
docs.text:
One decision for the whole certificate, one for the meet-table match; both compute to yes — that computation is the re-verification of every engine claim above.

open LatticeCheck 𝑭 𝑺

certOK : LatticeCertOK cert
certOK = from-yes (latticeCertOK? cert)

certMeet : MeetMatches 𝑭 𝑺 𝑳 cert
certMeet = from-yes (meetMatches? 𝑭 𝑺 𝑳 cert)

docs.title: The headline theorems
docs.text:
The target lattice is decidably representable, witnessed by this algebra; and the certificate's congruence list is a complete Layer-D enumeration of the algebra's decidable congruences.

SLR02-Representableᵈ : Representableᵈ (toLattice 𝑳)
SLR02-Representableᵈ = certRepresentableᵈ 𝑭 𝑺 𝑳 cert certOK certMeet

SLR02-FiniteCongruencesᵈ : FiniteCongruencesᵈ 𝑨
SLR02-FiniteCongruencesᵈ = certFiniteCongruencesᵈ cert certOK

open CertCheck 𝑭 𝑺 using ( arOf )

cert : LatticeCert 7 4 arOf 6

  where

         ∷ (0F ∷ 0F ∷ 0F ∷ 0F ∷ 0F ∷ 0F ∷ 0F ∷ [])
         ∷ []

  prinᵛ : Vec (Vec (Fin 6) 7) 7
  prinᵛ = (0F ∷ 2F ∷ 1F ∷ 2F ∷ 1F ∷ 5F ∷ 1F ∷ [])

docs.title: The verification
docs.text:
One decision for the whole certificate, one for the meet-table match; both compute to yes — that computation is the re-verification of every engine claim above.

open LatticeCheck 𝑭 𝑺

certOK : LatticeCertOK cert
certOK = from-yes (latticeCertOK? cert)

certMeet : MeetMatches 𝑭 𝑺 𝑳 cert
certMeet = from-yes (meetMatches? 𝑭 𝑺 𝑳 cert)

docs.title: The headline theorems
docs.text:
The target lattice is decidably representable, witnessed by this algebra; and the certificate's congruence list is a complete Layer-D enumeration of the algebra's decidable congruences.

SLR03-Representableᵈ : Representableᵈ (toLattice 𝑳)
SLR03-Representableᵈ = certRepresentableᵈ 𝑭 𝑺 𝑳 cert certOK certMeet

SLR03-FiniteCongruencesᵈ : FiniteCongruencesᵈ 𝑨
SLR03-FiniteCongruencesᵈ = certFiniteCongruencesᵈ cert certOK

docs.title: A machine-checked representation: Con(B4) ≅ manuscript L4
docs.text:
This is the FLRP.Certificates.SmallLatticeReps.SLR04 module of the Agda Universal Algebra Library.

This module was emitted by scripts/python/flrp/emit_agda.py from scripts/python/flrp/inputs/slr/slr04.json. Do not edit it by hand; rerun the emitter instead.

B4/L4 in the numbering of the DeMeo–Freese–Jipsen manuscript Representing Finite Lattices as Congruence Lattices of Finite Algebras (§ 6 of the 2016-06-10 draft, docs/papers/fin-lat-rep/SmallLatticeReps.tex). The dictionary between the manuscript's lattice numbering and this library's names is docs/notes/flrp-slr-naming.md.

It re-verifies, end-to-end through the WP-6 certificate pipeline (#457), the claim that the congruence lattice of the algebra "B4" — carrier size 4, unary operations f, g — is isomorphic to the lattice "manuscript L4" (6 elements). The engine's output below (normal-form parent vectors, Freese traces, and pointer tables) is certificate data only: the search-free checkers of Setoid.Congruences.Certificates re-verify all of it during type-checking, and the FLRP.Certificates assembly turns the checked certificate into the headline theorems — a Representableᵈ witness for the target lattice and a FiniteCongruencesᵈ instance for the algebra. Nothing is believed on the engine's authority: a wrong table or trace would make a decidable check compute to no and break compilation.

{-# OPTIONS --cubical-compatible --exact-split --safe #-}

module FLRP.Certificates.SmallLatticeReps.SLR04 where

-- Imports from Agda and the Agda Standard Library -----------------------------
open import Data.Fin.Base       using ( Fin )
open import Data.Fin.Patterns   using ( 0F ; 1F ; 2F ; 3F ; 4F ; 5F )

-- Imports from the Agda Universal Algebra Library -----------------------------

open import Classical.Structures.Unary   using ( tablesToUnaryAlgebra
                                               ; tablesToUnaryAlgebra-FiniteAlgebra
                                               ; Sig-Unary-Fin-FiniteSignature )
open import FLRP.Certificates            using ( MeetMatches ; meetMatches?
                                               ; certRepresentableᵈ )
open import FLRP.Problem                 using ( FiniteLattice ; toLattice )
open import FLRP.Representable           using ( Representableᵈ )
open import Overture.Cayley              using ( Table ; ⟦_⟧ ; from-yes )
open import Overture.Operations.Properties
                                         using ( Associative? ; Commutative?
                                               ; Idempotent? ; Absorbsˡ? ; Absorbsʳ? )
open import Setoid.Algebras.Basic        using ( Algebra )
open import Setoid.Algebras.Finite       using ( FiniteAlgebra )
open import Setoid.Congruences.Certificates.Schema
                                         using ( ParentVec ; Trace ; LatticeCert
                                               ; mkLatticeCert ; mkMerge
                                               ; seed ; translate )
open import Setoid.Congruences.Certificates.Congruence
                                         using ( module CertCheck )

docs.title: The algebra, from its operation tables
docs.text:
Row f of opTables is the value table of the f-th unary operation; Classical.Structures.Unary turns the table into the algebra and its finiteness witnesses.

opTables : Vec (Vec (Fin 4) 4) 2
opTables = (1F ∷ 0F ∷ 3F ∷ 2F ∷ [])
         ∷ (0F ∷ 0F ∷ 2F ∷ 2F ∷ [])
         ∷ []

𝑨 : Algebra {𝑆 = Sig-Unary (Fin 2)} 0ℓ 0ℓ
𝑨 = tablesToUnaryAlgebra 4 2 opTables

𝑭 : FiniteAlgebra 𝑨
𝑭 = tablesToUnaryAlgebra-FiniteAlgebra 4 2 opTables

𝑺 : FiniteSignature (Sig-Unary (Fin 2))
𝑺 = Sig-Unary-Fin-FiniteSignature 2

docs.title: The target lattice, from its Cayley tables
docs.text:
The claimed congruence lattice "manuscript L4", presented exactly as the worked lattice examples are (Examples.Classical.Lattices.L7): meet and join tables, every law discharged by decision over the finite carrier.

∧-table ∨-table : Table 6
∧-table = (0F ∷ 0F ∷ 0F ∷ 0F ∷ 0F ∷ 0F ∷ [])
        ∷ (0F ∷ 1F ∷ 0F ∷ 0F ∷ 1F ∷ 1F ∷ [])
        ∷ (0F ∷ 0F ∷ 2F ∷ 0F ∷ 2F ∷ 2F ∷ [])
        ∷ (0F ∷ 0F ∷ 0F ∷ 3F ∷ 0F ∷ 3F ∷ [])
        ∷ (0F ∷ 1F ∷ 2F ∷ 0F ∷ 4F ∷ 4F ∷ [])
        ∷ (0F ∷ 1F ∷ 2F ∷ 3F ∷ 4F ∷ 5F ∷ [])
        ∷ []

∨-table = (0F ∷ 1F ∷ 2F ∷ 3F ∷ 4F ∷ 5F ∷ [])
        ∷ (1F ∷ 1F ∷ 4F ∷ 5F ∷ 4F ∷ 5F ∷ [])
        ∷ (2F ∷ 4F ∷ 2F ∷ 5F ∷ 4F ∷ 5F ∷ [])
        ∷ (3F ∷ 5F ∷ 5F ∷ 3F ∷ 5F ∷ 5F ∷ [])
        ∷ (4F ∷ 4F ∷ 4F ∷ 5F ∷ 4F ∷ 5F ∷ [])
        ∷ (5F ∷ 5F ∷ 5F ∷ 5F ∷ 5F ∷ 5F ∷ [])
        ∷ []

open FiniteLattice

𝑳 : FiniteLattice
𝑳 .size     = 5
𝑳 ._∧_      = ⟦ ∧-table ⟧
𝑳 ._∨_      = ⟦ ∨-table ⟧
𝑳 .∧-assoc  = from-yes (Associative? ⟦ ∧-table ⟧)
𝑳 .∧-comm   = from-yes (Commutative? ⟦ ∧-table ⟧)
𝑳 .∧-idem   = from-yes (Idempotent? ⟦ ∧-table ⟧)
𝑳 .∨-assoc  = from-yes (Associative? ⟦ ∨-table ⟧)
𝑳 .∨-comm   = from-yes (Commutative? ⟦ ∨-table ⟧)
𝑳 .∨-idem   = from-yes (Idempotent? ⟦ ∨-table ⟧)
𝑳 .absorbˡ  = from-yes (Absorbsˡ? ⟦ ∧-table ⟧ ⟦ ∨-table ⟧)
𝑳 .absorbʳ  = from-yes (Absorbsʳ? ⟦ ∧-table ⟧ ⟦ ∨-table ⟧)

docs.title: The certificate
docs.text:
The engine's whole-lattice certificate (design note § 4): the congruence list as normal-form parent vectors, indexed by the lattice's carrier; the principal-congruence pointer table with one Freese trace per carrier pair; and the join traces, seeded by forest edges. The meet and join tables are the target's own tables, which is what MeetMatches pins.

open CertCheck 𝑭 𝑺 using ( arOf )

cert : LatticeCert 4 2 arOf 6
cert = mkLatticeCert partsᵛ 0F prinᵛ prinTrᵛ ∧-table ∨-table joinTrᵛ
  where

docs.title: The verification
docs.text:
One decision for the whole certificate, one for the meet-table match; both compute to yes — that computation is the re-verification of every engine claim above.

open LatticeCheck 𝑭 𝑺

certOK : LatticeCertOK cert
certOK = from-yes (latticeCertOK? cert)

certMeet : MeetMatches 𝑭 𝑺 𝑳 cert
certMeet = from-yes (meetMatches? 𝑭 𝑺 𝑳 cert)

docs.title: The headline theorems
docs.text:
The target lattice is decidably representable, witnessed by this algebra; and the certificate's congruence list is a complete Layer-D enumeration of the algebra's decidable congruences.

SLR04-Representableᵈ : Representableᵈ (toLattice 𝑳)
SLR04-Representableᵈ = certRepresentableᵈ 𝑭 𝑺 𝑳 cert certOK certMeet

SLR04-FiniteCongruencesᵈ : FiniteCongruencesᵈ 𝑨
SLR04-FiniteCongruencesᵈ = certFiniteCongruencesᵈ cert certOK

docs.title: A machine-checked representation: Con(B5) ≅ manuscript L5
docs.text:
This is the FLRP.Certificates.SmallLatticeReps.SLR05 module of the Agda Universal Algebra Library.

This module was emitted by scripts/python/flrp/emit_agda.py from scripts/python/flrp/inputs/slr/slr05.json. Do not edit it by hand; rerun the emitter instead.

B5/L5 in the numbering of the DeMeo–Freese–Jipsen manuscript Representing Finite Lattices as Congruence Lattices of Finite Algebras (§ 6 of the 2016-06-10 draft, docs/papers/fin-lat-rep/SmallLatticeReps.tex). The dictionary between the manuscript's lattice numbering and this library's names is docs/notes/flrp-slr-naming.md.

It re-verifies, end-to-end through the WP-6 certificate pipeline (#457), the claim that the congruence lattice of the algebra "B5" — carrier size 12, unary operations f, g, h — is isomorphic to the lattice "manuscript L5" (6 elements). The engine's output below (normal-form parent vectors, Freese traces, and pointer tables) is certificate data only: the search-free checkers of Setoid.Congruences.Certificates re-verify all of it during type-checking, and the FLRP.Certificates assembly turns the checked certificate into the headline theorems — a Representableᵈ witness for the target lattice and a FiniteCongruencesᵈ instance for the algebra. Nothing is believed on the engine's authority: a wrong table or trace would make a decidable check compute to no and break compilation.

{-# OPTIONS --cubical-compatible --exact-split --safe #-}

docs.title: The algebra, from its operation tables
docs.text:
Row f of opTables is the value table of the f-th unary operation; Classical.Structures.Unary turns the table into the algebra and its finiteness witnesses.

opTables : Vec (Vec (Fin 12) 12) 3
opTables = (1F ∷ 2F ∷ 3F ∷ 4F ∷ 5F ∷ 0F ∷ 7F ∷ 8F ∷ 9F ∷ 10F ∷ 11F ∷ 6F ∷ [])
         ∷ (6F ∷ 11F ∷ 10F ∷ 9F ∷ 8F ∷ 7F ∷ 0F ∷ 5F ∷ 4F ∷ 3F ∷ 2F ∷ 1F ∷ [])
         ∷ (0F ∷ 0F ∷ 0F ∷ 6F ∷ 0F ∷ 0F ∷ 0F ∷ 0F ∷ 6F ∷ 0F ∷ 0F ∷ 0F ∷ [])
         ∷ []

𝑨 : Algebra {𝑆 = Sig-Unary (Fin 3)} 0ℓ 0ℓ
𝑨 = tablesToUnaryAlgebra 12 3 opTables

𝑭 : FiniteAlgebra 𝑨
𝑭 = tablesToUnaryAlgebra-FiniteAlgebra 12 3 opTables

𝑺 : FiniteSignature (Sig-Unary (Fin 3))
𝑺 = Sig-Unary-Fin-FiniteSignature 3

docs.title: The target lattice, from its Cayley tables
docs.text:
The claimed congruence lattice "manuscript L5", presented exactly as the worked lattice examples are (Examples.Classical.Lattices.L7): meet and join tables, every law discharged by decision over the finite carrier.

∧-table ∨-table : Table 6
∧-table = (0F ∷ 0F ∷ 0F ∷ 0F ∷ 0F ∷ 0F ∷ [])
        ∷ (0F ∷ 1F ∷ 0F ∷ 1F ∷ 1F ∷ 1F ∷ [])

        ∷ (0F ∷ 1F ∷ 0F ∷ 3F ∷ 1F ∷ 3F ∷ [])

𝑳 : FiniteLattice
𝑳 .size     = 5
𝑳 ._∧_      = ⟦ ∧-table ⟧
𝑳 ._∨_      = ⟦ ∨-table ⟧

docs.title: The verification
docs.text:
One decision for the whole certificate, one for the meet-table match; both compute to yes — that computation is the re-verification of every engine claim above.

open LatticeCheck 𝑭 𝑺

certOK : LatticeCertOK cert
certOK = from-yes (latticeCertOK? cert)

certMeet : MeetMatches 𝑭 𝑺 𝑳 cert
certMeet = from-yes (meetMatches? 𝑭 𝑺 𝑳 cert)

docs.title: The headline theorems
docs.text:
The target lattice is decidably representable, witnessed by this algebra; and the certificate's congruence list is a complete Layer-D enumeration of the algebra's decidable congruences.

SLR05-Representableᵈ : Representableᵈ (toLattice 𝑳)
SLR05-Representableᵈ = certRepresentableᵈ 𝑭 𝑺 𝑳 cert certOK certMeet

SLR05-FiniteCongruencesᵈ : FiniteCongruencesᵈ 𝑨
SLR05-FiniteCongruencesᵈ = certFiniteCongruencesᵈ cert certOK

docs.title: A machine-checked representation: Con(B6) ≅ manuscript L6 (the hexagon)
docs.text:
This is the FLRP.Certificates.SmallLatticeReps.SLR06 module of the Agda Universal Algebra Library.

This module was emitted by scripts/python/flrp/emit_agda.py from scripts/python/flrp/inputs/slr/slr06.json. Do not edit it by hand; rerun the emitter instead.

B6/L6 in the numbering of the DeMeo–Freese–Jipsen manuscript Representing Finite Lattices as Congruence Lattices of Finite Algebras (§ 6 of the 2016-06-10 draft, docs/papers/fin-lat-rep/SmallLatticeReps.tex). The dictionary between the manuscript's lattice numbering and this library's names is docs/notes/flrp-slr-naming.md.

It re-verifies, end-to-end through the WP-6 certificate pipeline (#457), the claim that the congruence lattice of the algebra "B6" — carrier size 6, unary operations f, g, h — is isomorphic to the lattice "manuscript L6 (the hexagon)" (6 elements). The engine's output below (normal-form parent vectors, Freese traces, and pointer tables) is certificate data only: the search-free checkers of Setoid.Congruences.Certificates re-verify all of it during type-checking, and the FLRP.Certificates assembly turns the checked certificate into the headline theorems — a Representableᵈ witness for the target lattice and a FiniteCongruencesᵈ instance for the algebra. Nothing is believed on the engine's authority: a wrong table or trace would make a decidable check compute to no and break compilation.

docs.title: The algebra, from its operation tables
docs.text:
Row f of opTables is the value table of the f-th unary operation; Classical.Structures.Unary turns the table into the algebra and its finiteness witnesses.

opTables : Vec (Vec (Fin 6) 6) 3
opTables = (2F ∷ 2F ∷ 1F ∷ 5F ∷ 5F ∷ 4F ∷ [])
         ∷ (3F ∷ 4F ∷ 4F ∷ 0F ∷ 1F ∷ 1F ∷ [])
         ∷ (4F ∷ 5F ∷ 3F ∷ 4F ∷ 5F ∷ 3F ∷ [])
         ∷ []

𝑨 : Algebra {𝑆 = Sig-Unary (Fin 3)} 0ℓ 0ℓ
𝑨 = tablesToUnaryAlgebra 6 3 opTables

𝑭 : FiniteAlgebra 𝑨
𝑭 = tablesToUnaryAlgebra-FiniteAlgebra 6 3 opTables

𝑺 : FiniteSignature (Sig-Unary (Fin 3))
𝑺 = Sig-Unary-Fin-FiniteSignature 3

docs.title: The target lattice, from its Cayley tables
docs.text:
The claimed congruence lattice "manuscript L6 (the hexagon)", presented exactly as the worked lattice examples are (Examples.Classical.Lattices.L7): meet and join tables, every law discharged by decision over the finite carrier.

∧-table ∨-table : Table 6
∧-table = (0F ∷ 0F ∷ 0F ∷ 0F ∷ 0F ∷ 0F ∷ [])
        ∷ (0F ∷ 1F ∷ 0F ∷ 1F ∷ 0F ∷ 1F ∷ [])
        ∷ (0F ∷ 0F ∷ 2F ∷ 0F ∷ 2F ∷ 2F ∷ [])
        ∷ (0F ∷ 1F ∷ 0F ∷ 3F ∷ 0F ∷ 3F ∷ [])
        ∷ (0F ∷ 0F ∷ 2F ∷ 0F ∷ 4F ∷ 4F ∷ [])
        ∷ (0F ∷ 1F ∷ 2F ∷ 3F ∷ 4F ∷ 5F ∷ [])
        ∷ []

∨-table = (0F ∷ 1F ∷ 2F ∷ 3F ∷ 4F ∷ 5F ∷ [])
        ∷ (1F ∷ 1F ∷ 5F ∷ 3F ∷ 5F ∷ 5F ∷ [])
        ∷ (2F ∷ 5F ∷ 2F ∷ 5F ∷ 4F ∷ 5F ∷ [])
        ∷ (3F ∷ 3F ∷ 5F ∷ 3F ∷ 5F ∷ 5F ∷ [])
        ∷ (4F ∷ 5F ∷ 4F ∷ 5F ∷ 4F ∷ 5F ∷ [])
        ∷ (5F ∷ 5F ∷ 5F ∷ 5F ∷ 5F ∷ 5F ∷ [])
        ∷ []

open FiniteLattice

𝑳 : FiniteLattice
𝑳 .size     = 5
𝑳 ._∧_      = ⟦ ∧-table ⟧
𝑳 ._∨_      = ⟦ ∨-table ⟧
𝑳 .∧-assoc  = from-yes (Associative? ⟦ ∧-table ⟧)
𝑳 .∧-comm   = from-yes (Commutative? ⟦ ∧-table ⟧)
𝑳 .∧-idem   = from-yes (Idempotent? ⟦ ∧-table ⟧)
𝑳 .∨-assoc  = from-yes (Associative? ⟦ ∨-table ⟧)
𝑳 .∨-comm   = from-yes (Commutative? ⟦ ∨-table ⟧)

docs.title: The verification
docs.text:
One decision for the whole certificate, one for the meet-table match; both compute to yes — that computation is the re-verification of every engine claim above.

open LatticeCheck 𝑭 𝑺

certOK : LatticeCertOK cert
certOK = from-yes (latticeCertOK? cert)

certMeet : MeetMatches 𝑭 𝑺 𝑳 cert
certMeet = from-yes (meetMatches? 𝑭 𝑺 𝑳 cert)

docs.title: The headline theorems
docs.text:
The target lattice is decidably representable, witnessed by this algebra; and the certificate's congruence list is a complete Layer-D enumeration of the algebra's decidable congruences.

SLR06-Representableᵈ : Representableᵈ (toLattice 𝑳)
SLR06-Representableᵈ = certRepresentableᵈ 𝑭 𝑺 𝑳 cert certOK certMeet

SLR06-FiniteCongruencesᵈ : FiniteCongruencesᵈ 𝑨
SLR06-FiniteCongruencesᵈ = certFiniteCongruencesᵈ cert certOK

docs.title: A machine-checked representation: Con(B7) ≅ manuscript L7
docs.text:
This is the FLRP.Certificates.SmallLatticeReps.SLR07 module of the Agda Universal Algebra Library.

This module was emitted by scripts/python/flrp/emit_agda.py from scripts/python/flrp/inputs/slr/slr07.json. Do not edit it by hand; rerun the emitter instead.

B7/L7 in the numbering of the DeMeo–Freese–Jipsen manuscript Representing Finite Lattices as Congruence Lattices of Finite Algebras (§ 6 of the 2016-06-10 draft, docs/papers/fin-lat-rep/SmallLatticeReps.tex). The dictionary between the manuscript's lattice numbering and this library's names is docs/notes/flrp-slr-naming.md.

It re-verifies, end-to-end through the WP-6 certificate pipeline (#457), the claim that the congruence lattice of the algebra "B7" — carrier size 6, unary operations f, g, h — is isomorphic to the lattice "manuscript L7" (6 elements). The engine's output below (normal-form parent vectors, Freese traces, and pointer tables) is certificate data only: the search-free checkers of Setoid.Congruences.Certificates re-verify all of it during type-checking, and the FLRP.Certificates assembly turns the checked certificate into the headline theorems — a Representableᵈ witness for the target lattice and a FiniteCongruencesᵈ instance for the algebra. Nothing is believed on the engine's authority: a wrong table or trace would make a decidable check compute to no and break compilation.

docs.title: The algebra, from its operation tables
docs.text:
Row f of opTables is the value table of the f-th unary operation; Classical.Structures.Unary turns the table into the algebra and its finiteness witnesses.

opTables : Vec (Vec (Fin 6) 6) 3
opTables = (1F ∷ 0F ∷ 0F ∷ 4F ∷ 3F ∷ 3F ∷ [])
         ∷ (4F ∷ 5F ∷ 5F ∷ 1F ∷ 2F ∷ 2F ∷ [])
         ∷ (3F ∷ 3F ∷ 4F ∷ 3F ∷ 3F ∷ 4F ∷ [])
         ∷ []

𝑨 : Algebra {𝑆 = Sig-Unary (Fin 3)} 0ℓ 0ℓ
𝑨 = tablesToUnaryAlgebra 6 3 opTables

𝑭 : FiniteAlgebra 𝑨
𝑭 = tablesToUnaryAlgebra-FiniteAlgebra 6 3 opTables

𝑺 : FiniteSignature (Sig-Unary (Fin 3))
𝑺 = Sig-Unary-Fin-FiniteSignature 3

docs.title: The target lattice, from its Cayley tables
docs.text:
The claimed congruence lattice "manuscript L7", presented exactly as the worked lattice examples are (Examples.Classical.Lattices.L7): meet and join tables, every law discharged by decision over the finite carrier.

∧-table ∨-table : Table 6
∧-table = (0F ∷ 0F ∷ 0F ∷ 0F ∷ 0F ∷ 0F ∷ [])
        ∷ (0F ∷ 1F ∷ 1F ∷ 0F ∷ 1F ∷ 1F ∷ [])
        ∷ (0F ∷ 1F ∷ 2F ∷ 0F ∷ 2F ∷ 2F ∷ [])
        ∷ (0F ∷ 0F ∷ 0F ∷ 3F ∷ 0F ∷ 3F ∷ [])
        ∷ (0F ∷ 1F ∷ 2F ∷ 0F ∷ 4F ∷ 4F ∷ [])
        ∷ (0F ∷ 1F ∷ 2F ∷ 3F ∷ 4F ∷ 5F ∷ [])
        ∷ []

∨-table = (0F ∷ 1F ∷ 2F ∷ 3F ∷ 4F ∷ 5F ∷ [])
        ∷ (1F ∷ 1F ∷ 2F ∷ 5F ∷ 4F ∷ 5F ∷ [])
        ∷ (2F ∷ 2F ∷ 2F ∷ 5F ∷ 4F ∷ 5F ∷ [])
        ∷ (3F ∷ 5F ∷ 5F ∷ 3F ∷ 5F ∷ 5F ∷ [])
        ∷ (4F ∷ 4F ∷ 4F ∷ 5F ∷ 4F ∷ 5F ∷ [])
        ∷ (5F ∷ 5F ∷ 5F ∷ 5F ∷ 5F ∷ 5F ∷ [])
        ∷ []

open FiniteLattice

𝑳 : FiniteLattice
𝑳 .size     = 5
𝑳 ._∧_      = ⟦ ∧-table ⟧
𝑳 ._∨_      = ⟦ ∨-table ⟧
𝑳 .∧-assoc  = from-yes (Associative? ⟦ ∧-table ⟧)
𝑳 .∧-comm   = from-yes (Commutative? ⟦ ∧-table ⟧)
𝑳 .∧-idem   = from-yes (Idempotent? ⟦ ∧-table ⟧)
𝑳 .∨-assoc  = from-yes (Associative? ⟦ ∨-table ⟧)
𝑳 .∨-comm   = from-yes (Commutative? ⟦ ∨-table ⟧)

docs.title: The verification
docs.text:
One decision for the whole certificate, one for the meet-table match; both compute to yes — that computation is the re-verification of every engine claim above.

open LatticeCheck 𝑭 𝑺

certOK : LatticeCertOK cert
certOK = from-yes (latticeCertOK? cert)

certMeet : MeetMatches 𝑭 𝑺 𝑳 cert
certMeet = from-yes (meetMatches? 𝑭 𝑺 𝑳 cert)

docs.title: The headline theorems
docs.text:
The target lattice is decidably representable, witnessed by this algebra; and the certificate's congruence list is a complete Layer-D enumeration of the algebra's decidable congruences.

SLR07-Representableᵈ : Representableᵈ (toLattice 𝑳)
SLR07-Representableᵈ = certRepresentableᵈ 𝑭 𝑺 𝑳 cert certOK certMeet

SLR07-FiniteCongruencesᵈ : FiniteCongruencesᵈ 𝑨
SLR07-FiniteCongruencesᵈ = certFiniteCongruencesᵈ cert certOK

docs.title: A machine-checked representation: Con(B8) ≅ manuscript L8 (M4)
docs.text:
This is the FLRP.Certificates.SmallLatticeReps.SLR08 module of the Agda Universal Algebra Library.

This module was emitted by scripts/python/flrp/emit_agda.py from scripts/python/flrp/inputs/slr/slr08.json. Do not edit it by hand; rerun the emitter instead.

B8/L8 in the numbering of the DeMeo–Freese–Jipsen manuscript Representing Finite Lattices as Congruence Lattices of Finite Algebras (§ 6 of the 2016-06-10 draft, docs/papers/fin-lat-rep/SmallLatticeReps.tex). The dictionary between the manuscript's lattice numbering and this library's names is docs/notes/flrp-slr-naming.md.

It re-verifies, end-to-end through the WP-6 certificate pipeline (#457), the claim that the congruence lattice of the algebra "B8" — carrier size 6, unary operations f, g — is isomorphic to the lattice "manuscript L8 (M4)" (6 elements). The engine's output below (normal-form parent vectors, Freese traces, and pointer tables) is certificate data only: the search-free checkers of Setoid.Congruences.Certificates re-verify all of it during type-checking, and the FLRP.Certificates assembly turns the checked certificate into the headline theorems — a Representableᵈ witness for the target lattice and a FiniteCongruencesᵈ instance for the algebra. Nothing is believed on the engine's authority: a wrong table or trace would make a decidable check compute to no and break compilation.

docs.title: The algebra, from its operation tables
docs.text:
Row f of opTables is the value table of the f-th unary operation; Classical.Structures.Unary turns the table into the algebra and its finiteness witnesses.

opTables : Vec (Vec (Fin 6) 6) 2

𝑺 : FiniteSignature (Sig-Unary (Fin 2))
𝑺 = Sig-Unary-Fin-FiniteSignature 2

docs.title: The target lattice, from its Cayley tables
docs.text:
The claimed congruence lattice "manuscript L8 (M4)", presented exactly as the worked lattice examples are (Examples.Classical.Lattices.L7): meet and join tables, every law discharged by decision over the finite carrier.

∧-table ∨-table : Table 6
∧-table = (0F ∷ 0F ∷ 0F ∷ 0F ∷ 0F ∷ 0F ∷ [])
        ∷ (0F ∷ 1F ∷ 0F ∷ 0F ∷ 0F ∷ 1F ∷ [])
        ∷ (0F ∷ 0F ∷ 2F ∷ 0F ∷ 0F ∷ 2F ∷ [])
        ∷ (0F ∷ 0F ∷ 0F ∷ 3F ∷ 0F ∷ 3F ∷ [])
        ∷ (0F ∷ 0F ∷ 0F ∷ 0F ∷ 4F ∷ 4F ∷ [])
        ∷ (0F ∷ 1F ∷ 2F ∷ 3F ∷ 4F ∷ 5F ∷ [])

𝑳 : FiniteLattice
𝑳 .size     = 5
𝑳 ._∧_      = ⟦ ∧-table ⟧

docs.title: The verification
docs.text:
One decision for the whole certificate, one for the meet-table match; both compute to yes — that computation is the re-verification of every engine claim above.

open LatticeCheck 𝑭 𝑺

certOK : LatticeCertOK cert
certOK = from-yes (latticeCertOK? cert)

certMeet : MeetMatches 𝑭 𝑺 𝑳 cert
certMeet = from-yes (meetMatches? 𝑭 𝑺 𝑳 cert)

docs.title: The headline theorems
docs.text:
The target lattice is decidably representable, witnessed by this algebra; and the certificate's congruence list is a complete Layer-D enumeration of the algebra's decidable congruences.

SLR08-Representableᵈ : Representableᵈ (toLattice 𝑳)
SLR08-Representableᵈ = certRepresentableᵈ 𝑭 𝑺 𝑳 cert certOK certMeet

SLR08-FiniteCongruencesᵈ : FiniteCongruencesᵈ 𝑨
SLR08-FiniteCongruencesᵈ = certFiniteCongruencesᵈ cert certOK

docs.title: A machine-checked representation: Con(B9) ≅ manuscript L9
docs.text:
This is the FLRP.Certificates.SmallLatticeReps.SLR09 module of the Agda Universal Algebra Library.

This module was emitted by scripts/python/flrp/emit_agda.py from scripts/python/flrp/inputs/slr/slr09.json. Do not edit it by hand; rerun the emitter instead.

B9/L9 in the numbering of the DeMeo–Freese–Jipsen manuscript Representing Finite Lattices as Congruence Lattices of Finite Algebras (§ 6 of the 2016-06-10 draft, docs/papers/fin-lat-rep/SmallLatticeReps.tex). The dictionary between the manuscript's lattice numbering and this library's names is docs/notes/flrp-slr-naming.md.

It re-verifies, end-to-end through the WP-6 certificate pipeline (#457), the claim that the congruence lattice of the algebra "B9" — carrier size 16, unary operations f, g, h — is isomorphic to the lattice "manuscript L9" (7 elements). The engine's output below (normal-form parent vectors, Freese traces, and pointer tables) is certificate data only: the search-free checkers of Setoid.Congruences.Certificates re-verify all of it during type-checking, and the FLRP.Certificates assembly turns the checked certificate into the headline theorems — a Representableᵈ witness for the target lattice and a FiniteCongruencesᵈ instance for the algebra. Nothing is believed on the engine's authority: a wrong table or trace would make a decidable check compute to no and break compilation.

{-# OPTIONS --cubical-compatible --exact-split --safe #-}

module FLRP.Certificates.SmallLatticeReps.SLR09 where

-- Imports from Agda and the Agda Standard Library -----------------------------
open import Data.Fin.Base       using ( Fin ; suc )
open import Data.Fin.Patterns   using ( 0F ; 1F ; 2F ; 3F ; 4F ; 5F ; 6F ; 7F ; 8F ; 9F )

-- Imports from the Agda Universal Algebra Library -----------------------------

                                               ; tablesToUnaryAlgebra-FiniteAlgebra
                                               ; Sig-Unary-Fin-FiniteSignature )
open import FLRP.Certificates            using ( MeetMatches ; meetMatches?
                                               ; certRepresentableᵈ )
open import FLRP.Problem                 using ( FiniteLattice ; toLattice )
open import FLRP.Representable           using ( Representableᵈ )
open import Overture.Cayley              using ( Table ; ⟦_⟧ ; from-yes )
open import Overture.Operations.Properties
                                         using ( Associative? ; Commutative?
                                               ; Idempotent? ; Absorbsˡ? ; Absorbsʳ? )
open import Setoid.Algebras.Basic        using ( Algebra )
open import Setoid.Algebras.Finite       using ( FiniteAlgebra )
open import Setoid.Congruences.Certificates.Schema
                                         using ( ParentVec ; Trace ; LatticeCert
                                               ; mkLatticeCert ; mkMerge

docs.text:
Row f of opTables is the value table of the f-th unary operation; Classical.Structures.Unary turns the table into the algebra and its finiteness witnesses.

docs.text:
The claimed congruence lattice "manuscript L9", presented exactly as the worked lattice examples are (Examples.Classical.Lattices.L7): meet and join tables, every law discharged by decision over the finite carrier.

docs.title: The verification
docs.text:
One decision for the whole certificate, one for the meet-table match; both compute to yes — that computation is the re-verification of every engine claim above.

open LatticeCheck 𝑭 𝑺

certOK : LatticeCertOK cert
certOK = from-yes (latticeCertOK? cert)

certMeet : MeetMatches 𝑭 𝑺 𝑳 cert
certMeet = from-yes (meetMatches? 𝑭 𝑺 𝑳 cert)

docs.title: The headline theorems
docs.text:
The target lattice is decidably representable, witnessed by this algebra; and the certificate's congruence list is a complete Layer-D enumeration of the algebra's decidable congruences.

SLR09-Representableᵈ : Representableᵈ (toLattice 𝑳)
SLR09-Representableᵈ = certRepresentableᵈ 𝑭 𝑺 𝑳 cert certOK certMeet

SLR09-FiniteCongruencesᵈ : FiniteCongruencesᵈ 𝑨
SLR09-FiniteCongruencesᵈ = certFiniteCongruencesᵈ cert certOK

docs.title: A machine-checked representation: Con(B12) ≅ manuscript L12
docs.text:
This is the FLRP.Certificates.SmallLatticeReps.SLR12 module of the Agda Universal Algebra Library.

This module was emitted by scripts/python/flrp/emit_agda.py from scripts/python/flrp/inputs/slr/slr12.json. Do not edit it by hand; rerun the emitter instead.

B12/L12 in the numbering of the DeMeo–Freese–Jipsen manuscript Representing Finite Lattices as Congruence Lattices of Finite Algebras (§ 6 of the 2016-06-10 draft, docs/papers/fin-lat-rep/SmallLatticeReps.tex). The dictionary between the manuscript's lattice numbering and this library's names is docs/notes/flrp-slr-naming.md.

It re-verifies, end-to-end through the WP-6 certificate pipeline (#457), the claim that the congruence lattice of the algebra "B12" — carrier size 9, unary operations f, g, h, k, l — is isomorphic to the lattice "manuscript L12" (7 elements). The engine's output below (normal-form parent vectors, Freese traces, and pointer tables) is certificate data only: the search-free checkers of Setoid.Congruences.Certificates re-verify all of it during type-checking, and the FLRP.Certificates assembly turns the checked certificate into the headline theorems — a Representableᵈ witness for the target lattice and a FiniteCongruencesᵈ instance for the algebra. Nothing is believed on the engine's authority: a wrong table or trace would make a decidable check compute to no and break compilation.

{-# OPTIONS --cubical-compatible --exact-split --safe #-}

module FLRP.Certificates.SmallLatticeReps.SLR12 where

-- Imports from Agda and the Agda Standard Library -----------------------------

open import Data.Fin.Patterns   using ( 0F ; 1F ; 2F ; 3F ; 4F ; 5F ; 6F ; 7F ; 8F )

-- Imports from the Agda Universal Algebra Library -----------------------------

open import Classical.Structures.Unary   using ( tablesToUnaryAlgebra
                                               ; tablesToUnaryAlgebra-FiniteAlgebra
                                               ; Sig-Unary-Fin-FiniteSignature )
open import FLRP.Certificates            using ( MeetMatches ; meetMatches?
                                               ; certRepresentableᵈ )
open import FLRP.Problem                 using ( FiniteLattice ; toLattice )
open import FLRP.Representable           using ( Representableᵈ )
open import Overture.Cayley              using ( Table ; ⟦_⟧ ; from-yes )
open import Overture.Operations.Properties
                                         using ( Associative? ; Commutative?
                                               ; Idempotent? ; Absorbsˡ? ; Absorbsʳ? )
open import Setoid.Algebras.Basic        using ( Algebra )
open import Setoid.Algebras.Finite       using ( FiniteAlgebra )
open import Setoid.Congruences.Certificates.Schema
                                         using ( ParentVec ; Trace ; LatticeCert
                                               ; mkLatticeCert ; mkMerge
                                               ; seed ; translate )
open import Setoid.Congruences.Certificates.Congruence
                                         using ( module CertCheck )

docs.title: The algebra, from its operation tables
docs.text:
Row f of opTables is the value table of the f-th unary operation; Classical.Structures.Unary turns the table into the algebra and its finiteness witnesses.

opTables : Vec (Vec (Fin 9) 9) 5
opTables = (0F ∷ 0F ∷ 3F ∷ 3F ∷ 3F ∷ 6F ∷ 6F ∷ 6F ∷ 0F ∷ [])
         ∷ (0F ∷ 0F ∷ 8F ∷ 8F ∷ 8F ∷ 1F ∷ 1F ∷ 1F ∷ 0F ∷ [])
         ∷ (0F ∷ 5F ∷ 5F ∷ 4F ∷ 0F ∷ 0F ∷ 5F ∷ 4F ∷ 4F ∷ [])
         ∷ (4F ∷ 2F ∷ 2F ∷ 3F ∷ 4F ∷ 4F ∷ 2F ∷ 3F ∷ 3F ∷ [])
         ∷ (5F ∷ 5F ∷ 7F ∷ 7F ∷ 7F ∷ 6F ∷ 6F ∷ 6F ∷ 5F ∷ [])
         ∷ []

𝑨 : Algebra {𝑆 = Sig-Unary (Fin 5)} 0ℓ 0ℓ
𝑨 = tablesToUnaryAlgebra 9 5 opTables

𝑭 : FiniteAlgebra 𝑨
𝑭 = tablesToUnaryAlgebra-FiniteAlgebra 9 5 opTables

𝑺 : FiniteSignature (Sig-Unary (Fin 5))
𝑺 = Sig-Unary-Fin-FiniteSignature 5

docs.title: The target lattice, from its Cayley tables
docs.text:
The claimed congruence lattice "manuscript L12", presented exactly as the worked lattice examples are (Examples.Classical.Lattices.L7): meet and join tables, every law discharged by decision over the finite carrier.

docs.title: The certificate
docs.text:
The engine's whole-lattice certificate (design note § 4): the congruence list as normal-form parent vectors, indexed by the lattice's carrier; the principal-congruence pointer table with one Freese trace per carrier pair; and the join traces, seeded by forest edges. The meet and join tables are the target's own tables, which is what MeetMatches pins.

docs.title: The verification
docs.text:
One decision for the whole certificate, one for the meet-table match; both compute to yes — that computation is the re-verification of every engine claim above.

open LatticeCheck 𝑭 𝑺

certOK : LatticeCertOK cert
certOK = from-yes (latticeCertOK? cert)

certMeet : MeetMatches 𝑭 𝑺 𝑳 cert
certMeet = from-yes (meetMatches? 𝑭 𝑺 𝑳 cert)

docs.title: The headline theorems
docs.text:
The target lattice is decidably representable, witnessed by this algebra; and the certificate's congruence list is a complete Layer-D enumeration of the algebra's decidable congruences.

SLR12-Representableᵈ : Representableᵈ (toLattice 𝑳)
SLR12-Representableᵈ = certRepresentableᵈ 𝑭 𝑺 𝑳 cert certOK certMeet

SLR12-FiniteCongruencesᵈ : FiniteCongruencesᵈ 𝑨
SLR12-FiniteCongruencesᵈ = certFiniteCongruencesᵈ cert certOK

docs.title: A machine-checked representation: Con(B13) ≅ manuscript L13
docs.text:
This is the FLRP.Certificates.SmallLatticeReps.SLR13 module of the Agda Universal Algebra Library.

This module was emitted by scripts/python/flrp/emit_agda.py from scripts/python/flrp/inputs/slr/slr13.json. Do not edit it by hand; rerun the emitter instead.

B13/L13 in the numbering of the DeMeo–Freese–Jipsen manuscript Representing Finite Lattices as Congruence Lattices of Finite Algebras (§ 6 of the 2016-06-10 draft, docs/papers/fin-lat-rep/SmallLatticeReps.tex). The dictionary between the manuscript's lattice numbering and this library's names is docs/notes/flrp-slr-naming.md.

It re-verifies, end-to-end through the WP-6 certificate pipeline (#457), the claim that the congruence lattice of the algebra "B13" — carrier size 19, unary operations f, g, h, k, l — is isomorphic to the lattice "manuscript L13" (7 elements). The engine's output below (normal-form parent vectors, Freese traces, and pointer tables) is certificate data only: the search-free checkers of Setoid.Congruences.Certificates re-verify all of it during type-checking, and the FLRP.Certificates assembly turns the checked certificate into the headline theorems — a Representableᵈ witness for the target lattice and a FiniteCongruencesᵈ instance for the algebra. Nothing is believed on the engine's authority: a wrong table or trace would make a decidable check compute to no and break compilation.

docs.title: The verification
docs.text:
One decision for the whole certificate, one for the meet-table match; both compute to yes — that computation is the re-verification of every engine claim above.

open LatticeCheck 𝑭 𝑺

certOK : LatticeCertOK cert
certOK = from-yes (latticeCertOK? cert)

certMeet : MeetMatches 𝑭 𝑺 𝑳 cert
certMeet = from-yes (meetMatches? 𝑭 𝑺 𝑳 cert)

docs.title: The headline theorems
docs.text:
The target lattice is decidably representable, witnessed by this algebra; and the certificate's congruence list is a complete Layer-D enumeration of the algebra's decidable congruences.

SLR13-Representableᵈ : Representableᵈ (toLattice 𝑳)
SLR13-Representableᵈ = certRepresentableᵈ 𝑭 𝑺 𝑳 cert certOK certMeet

SLR13-FiniteCongruencesᵈ : FiniteCongruencesᵈ 𝑨
SLR13-FiniteCongruencesᵈ = certFiniteCongruencesᵈ cert certOK

docs.title: A machine-checked representation: Con(B15) ≅ manuscript L15
docs.text:
This is the FLRP.Certificates.SmallLatticeReps.SLR15 module of the Agda Universal Algebra Library.

This module was emitted by scripts/python/flrp/emit_agda.py from scripts/python/flrp/inputs/slr/slr15.json. Do not edit it by hand; rerun the emitter instead.

B15/L15 in the numbering of the DeMeo–Freese–Jipsen manuscript Representing Finite Lattices as Congruence Lattices of Finite Algebras (§ 6 of the 2016-06-10 draft, docs/papers/fin-lat-rep/SmallLatticeReps.tex). The dictionary between the manuscript's lattice numbering and this library's names is docs/notes/flrp-slr-naming.md.

It re-verifies, end-to-end through the WP-6 certificate pipeline (#457), the claim that the congruence lattice of the algebra "B15" — carrier size 4, unary operations f — is isomorphic to the lattice "manuscript L15" (7 elements). The engine's output below (normal-form parent vectors, Freese traces, and pointer tables) is certificate data only: the search-free checkers of Setoid.Congruences.Certificates re-verify all of it during type-checking, and the FLRP.Certificates assembly turns the checked certificate into the headline theorems — a Representableᵈ witness for the target lattice and a FiniteCongruencesᵈ instance for the algebra. Nothing is believed on the engine's authority: a wrong table or trace would make a decidable check compute to no and break compilation.

{-# OPTIONS --cubical-compatible --exact-split --safe #-}

module FLRP.Certificates.SmallLatticeReps.SLR15 where

-- Imports from Agda and the Agda Standard Library -----------------------------
open import Data.Fin.Base       using ( Fin )
open import Data.Fin.Patterns   using ( 0F ; 1F ; 2F ; 3F ; 4F ; 5F ; 6F )
open import Data.List.Base      using ( [] ; _∷_ )
open import Data.Vec.Base       using ( Vec ; [] ; _∷_ )
open import Level               using ( 0ℓ )

-- Imports from the Agda Universal Algebra Library -----------------------------
open import Classical.Signatures.Unary   using ( Sig-Unary )
open import Classical.Structures.Unary   using ( tablesToUnaryAlgebra
                                               ; tablesToUnaryAlgebra-FiniteAlgebra
                                               ; Sig-Unary-Fin-FiniteSignature )
open import FLRP.Certificates            using ( MeetMatches ; meetMatches?
                                               ; certRepresentableᵈ )
open import FLRP.Problem                 using ( FiniteLattice ; toLattice )
open import FLRP.Representable           using ( Representableᵈ )
open import Overture.Cayley              using ( Table ; ⟦_⟧ ; from-yes )
open import Overture.Operations.Properties
                                         using ( Associative? ; Commutative?
                                               ; Idempotent? ; Absorbsˡ? ; Absorbsʳ? )
open import Setoid.Algebras.Basic        using ( Algebra )
open import Setoid.Algebras.Finite       using ( FiniteAlgebra )
open import Setoid.Congruences.Certificates.Schema
                                         using ( ParentVec ; Trace ; LatticeCert
                                               ; mkLatticeCert ; mkMerge
                                               ; seed ; translate )
open import Setoid.Congruences.Certificates.Congruence
                                         using ( module CertCheck )
open import Setoid.Congruences.Certificates.Lattice
                                         using ( module LatticeCheck )
open import Setoid.Congruences.Finite.Decidable
                                         using ( FiniteCongruencesᵈ )
open import Setoid.Signatures.Finite     using ( FiniteSignature )

docs.title: The algebra, from its operation tables
docs.text:
Row f of opTables is the value table of the f-th unary operation; Classical.Structures.Unary turns the table into the algebra and its finiteness witnesses.

opTables : Vec (Vec (Fin 4) 4) 1
opTables = (1F ∷ 0F ∷ 3F ∷ 2F ∷ [])
         ∷ []

𝑨 : Algebra {𝑆 = Sig-Unary (Fin 1)} 0ℓ 0ℓ
𝑨 = tablesToUnaryAlgebra 4 1 opTables

𝑭 : FiniteAlgebra 𝑨
𝑭 = tablesToUnaryAlgebra-FiniteAlgebra 4 1 opTables

𝑺 : FiniteSignature (Sig-Unary (Fin 1))
𝑺 = Sig-Unary-Fin-FiniteSignature 1

docs.title: The target lattice, from its Cayley tables
docs.text:
The claimed congruence lattice "manuscript L15", presented exactly as the worked lattice examples are (Examples.Classical.Lattices.L7): meet and join tables, every law discharged by decision over the finite carrier.

∧-table ∨-table : Table 7
∧-table = (0F ∷ 0F ∷ 0F ∷ 0F ∷ 0F ∷ 0F ∷ 0F ∷ [])
        ∷ (0F ∷ 1F ∷ 0F ∷ 0F ∷ 0F ∷ 1F ∷ 1F ∷ [])
        ∷ (0F ∷ 0F ∷ 2F ∷ 0F ∷ 0F ∷ 2F ∷ 2F ∷ [])
        ∷ (0F ∷ 0F ∷ 0F ∷ 3F ∷ 0F ∷ 0F ∷ 3F ∷ [])
        ∷ (0F ∷ 0F ∷ 0F ∷ 0F ∷ 4F ∷ 0F ∷ 4F ∷ [])
        ∷ (0F ∷ 1F ∷ 2F ∷ 0F ∷ 0F ∷ 5F ∷ 5F ∷ [])
        ∷ (0F ∷ 1F ∷ 2F ∷ 3F ∷ 4F ∷ 5F ∷ 6F ∷ [])
        ∷ []

∨-table = (0F ∷ 1F ∷ 2F ∷ 3F ∷ 4F ∷ 5F ∷ 6F ∷ [])
        ∷ (1F ∷ 1F ∷ 5F ∷ 6F ∷ 6F ∷ 5F ∷ 6F ∷ [])
        ∷ (2F ∷ 5F ∷ 2F ∷ 6F ∷ 6F ∷ 5F ∷ 6F ∷ [])
        ∷ (3F ∷ 6F ∷ 6F ∷ 3F ∷ 6F ∷ 6F ∷ 6F ∷ [])
        ∷ (4F ∷ 6F ∷ 6F ∷ 6F ∷ 4F ∷ 6F ∷ 6F ∷ [])
        ∷ (5F ∷ 5F ∷ 5F ∷ 6F ∷ 6F ∷ 5F ∷ 6F ∷ [])
        ∷ (6F ∷ 6F ∷ 6F ∷ 6F ∷ 6F ∷ 6F ∷ 6F ∷ [])
        ∷ []

open FiniteLattice

𝑳 : FiniteLattice
𝑳 .size     = 6
𝑳 ._∧_      = ⟦ ∧-table ⟧
𝑳 ._∨_      = ⟦ ∨-table ⟧
𝑳 .∧-assoc  = from-yes (Associative? ⟦ ∧-table ⟧)
𝑳 .∧-comm   = from-yes (Commutative? ⟦ ∧-table ⟧)
𝑳 .∧-idem   = from-yes (Idempotent? ⟦ ∧-table ⟧)
𝑳 .∨-assoc  = from-yes (Associative? ⟦ ∨-table ⟧)
𝑳 .∨-comm   = from-yes (Commutative? ⟦ ∨-table ⟧)
𝑳 .∨-idem   = from-yes (Idempotent? ⟦ ∨-table ⟧)
𝑳 .absorbˡ  = from-yes (Absorbsˡ? ⟦ ∧-table ⟧ ⟦ ∨-table ⟧)
𝑳 .absorbʳ  = from-yes (Absorbsʳ? ⟦ ∧-table ⟧ ⟦ ∨-table ⟧)

docs.title: The certificate
docs.text:
The engine's whole-lattice certificate (design note § 4): the congruence list as normal-form parent vectors, indexed by the lattice's carrier; the principal-congruence pointer table with one Freese trace per carrier pair; and the join traces, seeded by forest edges. The meet and join tables are the target's own tables, which is what MeetMatches pins.

open CertCheck 𝑭 𝑺 using ( arOf )

cert : LatticeCert 4 1 arOf 7
cert = mkLatticeCert partsᵛ 0F prinᵛ prinTrᵛ ∧-table ∨-table joinTrᵛ
  where
  partsᵛ : Vec (ParentVec 4) 7
  partsᵛ = (0F ∷ 1F ∷ 2F ∷ 3F ∷ [])
         ∷ (0F ∷ 0F ∷ 2F ∷ 3F ∷ [])
         ∷ (0F ∷ 1F ∷ 2F ∷ 2F ∷ [])
         ∷ (0F ∷ 1F ∷ 0F ∷ 1F ∷ [])
         ∷ (0F ∷ 1F ∷ 1F ∷ 0F ∷ [])
         ∷ (0F ∷ 0F ∷ 2F ∷ 2F ∷ [])
         ∷ (0F ∷ 0F ∷ 0F ∷ 0F ∷ [])
         ∷ []

  prinᵛ : Vec (Vec (Fin 7) 4) 4
  prinᵛ = (0F ∷ 1F ∷ 3F ∷ 4F ∷ [])
        ∷ (1F ∷ 0F ∷ 4F ∷ 3F ∷ [])
        ∷ (3F ∷ 4F ∷ 0F ∷ 2F ∷ [])
        ∷ (4F ∷ 3F ∷ 2F ∷ 0F ∷ [])
        ∷ []

  prinTrᵛ : Vec (Vec (Trace 4 1 arOf) 4) 4
  prinTrᵛ = ( []
            ∷ (mkMerge 0F 1F (seed 0) ∷ [])
            ∷ ( mkMerge 0F 2F (seed 0)
              ∷ mkMerge 1F 3F (translate 0F 0F (0F ∷ []) 0)
              ∷ [] )
            ∷ ( mkMerge 0F 3F (seed 0)
              ∷ mkMerge 1F 2F (translate 0F 0F (0F ∷ []) 0)
              ∷ [] )
            ∷ [] )
          ∷ ( (mkMerge 1F 0F (seed 0) ∷ [])
            ∷ []
            ∷ ( mkMerge 1F 2F (seed 0)

docs.title: The verification
docs.text:
One decision for the whole certificate, one for the meet-table match; both compute to yes — that computation is the re-verification of every engine claim above.

open LatticeCheck 𝑭 𝑺

certOK : LatticeCertOK cert
certOK = from-yes (latticeCertOK? cert)

certMeet : MeetMatches 𝑭 𝑺 𝑳 cert
certMeet = from-yes (meetMatches? 𝑭 𝑺 𝑳 cert)

docs.title: The headline theorems
docs.text:
The target lattice is decidably representable, witnessed by this algebra; and the certificate's congruence list is a complete Layer-D enumeration of the algebra's decidable congruences.

SLR15-Representableᵈ : Representableᵈ (toLattice 𝑳)
SLR15-Representableᵈ = certRepresentableᵈ 𝑭 𝑺 𝑳 cert certOK certMeet

SLR15-FiniteCongruencesᵈ : FiniteCongruencesᵈ 𝑨
SLR15-FiniteCongruencesᵈ = certFiniteCongruencesᵈ cert certOK

docs.title: A machine-checked representation: Con(B17) ≅ manuscript L17
docs.text:
This is the FLRP.Certificates.SmallLatticeReps.SLR17 module of the Agda Universal Algebra Library.

This module was emitted by scripts/python/flrp/emit_agda.py from scripts/python/flrp/inputs/slr/slr17.json. Do not edit it by hand; rerun the emitter instead.

B17/L17 in the numbering of the DeMeo–Freese–Jipsen manuscript Representing Finite Lattices as Congruence Lattices of Finite Algebras (§ 6 of the 2016-06-10 draft, docs/papers/fin-lat-rep/SmallLatticeReps.tex). The dictionary between the manuscript's lattice numbering and this library's names is docs/notes/flrp-slr-naming.md.

It re-verifies, end-to-end through the WP-6 certificate pipeline (#457), the claim that the congruence lattice of the algebra "B17" — carrier size 12, unary operations f, g, h — is isomorphic to the lattice "manuscript L17" (7 elements). The engine's output below (normal-form parent vectors, Freese traces, and pointer tables) is certificate data only: the search-free checkers of Setoid.Congruences.Certificates re-verify all of it during type-checking, and the FLRP.Certificates assembly turns the checked certificate into the headline theorems — a Representableᵈ witness for the target lattice and a FiniteCongruencesᵈ instance for the algebra. Nothing is believed on the engine's authority: a wrong table or trace would make a decidable check compute to no and break compilation.

{-# OPTIONS --cubical-compatible --exact-split --safe #-}

docs.title: The algebra, from its operation tables
docs.text:
Row f of opTables is the value table of the f-th unary operation; Classical.Structures.Unary turns the table into the algebra and its finiteness witnesses.

         ∷ []

docs.text:

docs.title: The verification
docs.text:
One decision for the whole certificate, one for the meet-table match; both compute to yes — that computation is the re-verification of every engine claim above.

open LatticeCheck 𝑭 𝑺

certOK : LatticeCertOK cert
certOK = from-yes (latticeCertOK? cert)

certMeet : MeetMatches 𝑭 𝑺 𝑳 cert
certMeet = from-yes (meetMatches? 𝑭 𝑺 𝑳 cert)

docs.title: The headline theorems
docs.text:
The target lattice is decidably representable, witnessed by this algebra; and the certificate's congruence list is a complete Layer-D enumeration of the algebra's decidable congruences.

SLR17-Representableᵈ : Representableᵈ (toLattice 𝑳)
SLR17-Representableᵈ = certRepresentableᵈ 𝑭 𝑺 𝑳 cert certOK certMeet

SLR17-FiniteCongruencesᵈ : FiniteCongruencesᵈ 𝑨
SLR17-FiniteCongruencesᵈ = certFiniteCongruencesᵈ cert certOK

docs.title: A machine-checked representation: Con(B19) ≅ manuscript L19
docs.text:
This is the FLRP.Certificates.SmallLatticeReps.SLR19 module of the Agda Universal Algebra Library.

This module was emitted by scripts/python/flrp/emit_agda.py from scripts/python/flrp/inputs/slr/slr19.json. Do not edit it by hand; rerun the emitter instead.

B19/L19 in the numbering of the DeMeo–Freese–Jipsen manuscript Representing Finite Lattices as Congruence Lattices of Finite Algebras (§ 6 of the 2016-06-10 draft, docs/papers/fin-lat-rep/SmallLatticeReps.tex). The dictionary between the manuscript's lattice numbering and this library's names is docs/notes/flrp-slr-naming.md.

It re-verifies, end-to-end through the WP-6 certificate pipeline (#457), the claim that the congruence lattice of the algebra "B19" — carrier size 8, unary operations f, g, h — is isomorphic to the lattice "manuscript L19" (7 elements). The engine's output below (normal-form parent vectors, Freese traces, and pointer tables) is certificate data only: the search-free checkers of Setoid.Congruences.Certificates re-verify all of it during type-checking, and the FLRP.Certificates assembly turns the checked certificate into the headline theorems — a Representableᵈ witness for the target lattice and a FiniteCongruencesᵈ instance for the algebra. Nothing is believed on the engine's authority: a wrong table or trace would make a decidable check compute to no and break compilation.

{-# OPTIONS --cubical-compatible --exact-split --safe #-}

module FLRP.Certificates.SmallLatticeReps.SLR19 where

-- Imports from Agda and the Agda Standard Library -----------------------------
open import Data.Fin.Base       using ( Fin )
open import Data.Fin.Patterns   using ( 0F ; 1F ; 2F ; 3F ; 4F ; 5F ; 6F ; 7F )

-- Imports from the Agda Universal Algebra Library -----------------------------

open import Classical.Structures.Unary   using ( tablesToUnaryAlgebra
                                               ; tablesToUnaryAlgebra-FiniteAlgebra
                                               ; Sig-Unary-Fin-FiniteSignature )
open import FLRP.Certificates            using ( MeetMatches ; meetMatches?
                                               ; certRepresentableᵈ )
open import FLRP.Problem                 using ( FiniteLattice ; toLattice )
open import FLRP.Representable           using ( Representableᵈ )
open import Overture.Cayley              using ( Table ; ⟦_⟧ ; from-yes )
open import Overture.Operations.Properties
                                         using ( Associative? ; Commutative?
                                               ; Idempotent? ; Absorbsˡ? ; Absorbsʳ? )
open import Setoid.Algebras.Basic        using ( Algebra )
open import Setoid.Algebras.Finite       using ( FiniteAlgebra )
open import Setoid.Congruences.Certificates.Schema
                                         using ( ParentVec ; Trace ; LatticeCert
                                               ; mkLatticeCert ; mkMerge
                                               ; seed ; translate )

docs.title: The algebra, from its operation tables
docs.text:
Row f of opTables is the value table of the f-th unary operation; Classical.Structures.Unary turns the table into the algebra and its finiteness witnesses.

opTables : Vec (Vec (Fin 8) 8) 3
opTables = (0F ∷ 1F ∷ 1F ∷ 0F ∷ 4F ∷ 5F ∷ 5F ∷ 4F ∷ [])
         ∷ (0F ∷ 2F ∷ 3F ∷ 1F ∷ 0F ∷ 2F ∷ 3F ∷ 1F ∷ [])
         ∷ (7F ∷ 6F ∷ 6F ∷ 7F ∷ 3F ∷ 2F ∷ 2F ∷ 3F ∷ [])
         ∷ []

𝑨 : Algebra {𝑆 = Sig-Unary (Fin 3)} 0ℓ 0ℓ
𝑨 = tablesToUnaryAlgebra 8 3 opTables

𝑭 : FiniteAlgebra 𝑨
𝑭 = tablesToUnaryAlgebra-FiniteAlgebra 8 3 opTables

𝑺 : FiniteSignature (Sig-Unary (Fin 3))
𝑺 = Sig-Unary-Fin-FiniteSignature 3

docs.title: The target lattice, from its Cayley tables
docs.text:
The claimed congruence lattice "manuscript L19", presented exactly as the worked lattice examples are (Examples.Classical.Lattices.L7): meet and join tables, every law discharged by decision over the finite carrier.

∧-table ∨-table : Table 7
∧-table = (0F ∷ 0F ∷ 0F ∷ 0F ∷ 0F ∷ 0F ∷ 0F ∷ [])
        ∷ (0F ∷ 1F ∷ 0F ∷ 0F ∷ 1F ∷ 0F ∷ 1F ∷ [])
        ∷ (0F ∷ 0F ∷ 2F ∷ 0F ∷ 0F ∷ 2F ∷ 2F ∷ [])
        ∷ (0F ∷ 0F ∷ 0F ∷ 3F ∷ 0F ∷ 3F ∷ 3F ∷ [])
        ∷ (0F ∷ 1F ∷ 0F ∷ 0F ∷ 4F ∷ 0F ∷ 4F ∷ [])
        ∷ (0F ∷ 0F ∷ 2F ∷ 3F ∷ 0F ∷ 5F ∷ 5F ∷ [])
        ∷ (0F ∷ 1F ∷ 2F ∷ 3F ∷ 4F ∷ 5F ∷ 6F ∷ [])
        ∷ []

∨-table = (0F ∷ 1F ∷ 2F ∷ 3F ∷ 4F ∷ 5F ∷ 6F ∷ [])
        ∷ (1F ∷ 1F ∷ 6F ∷ 6F ∷ 4F ∷ 6F ∷ 6F ∷ [])
        ∷ (2F ∷ 6F ∷ 2F ∷ 5F ∷ 6F ∷ 5F ∷ 6F ∷ [])
        ∷ (3F ∷ 6F ∷ 5F ∷ 3F ∷ 6F ∷ 5F ∷ 6F ∷ [])
        ∷ (4F ∷ 4F ∷ 6F ∷ 6F ∷ 4F ∷ 6F ∷ 6F ∷ [])
        ∷ (5F ∷ 6F ∷ 5F ∷ 5F ∷ 6F ∷ 5F ∷ 6F ∷ [])
        ∷ (6F ∷ 6F ∷ 6F ∷ 6F ∷ 6F ∷ 6F ∷ 6F ∷ [])
        ∷ []

open FiniteLattice

𝑳 : FiniteLattice
𝑳 .size     = 6
𝑳 ._∧_      = ⟦ ∧-table ⟧
𝑳 ._∨_      = ⟦ ∨-table ⟧
𝑳 .∧-assoc  = from-yes (Associative? ⟦ ∧-table ⟧)
𝑳 .∧-comm   = from-yes (Commutative? ⟦ ∧-table ⟧)
𝑳 .∧-idem   = from-yes (Idempotent? ⟦ ∧-table ⟧)
𝑳 .∨-assoc  = from-yes (Associative? ⟦ ∨-table ⟧)
𝑳 .∨-comm   = from-yes (Commutative? ⟦ ∨-table ⟧)
𝑳 .∨-idem   = from-yes (Idempotent? ⟦ ∨-table ⟧)
𝑳 .absorbˡ  = from-yes (Absorbsˡ? ⟦ ∧-table ⟧ ⟦ ∨-table ⟧)

docs.title: The certificate
docs.text:
The engine's whole-lattice certificate (design note § 4): the congruence list as normal-form parent vectors, indexed by the lattice's carrier; the principal-congruence pointer table with one Freese trace per carrier pair; and the join traces, seeded by forest edges. The meet and join tables are the target's own tables, which is what MeetMatches pins.

open CertCheck 𝑭 𝑺 using ( arOf )

cert : LatticeCert 8 3 arOf 7
cert = mkLatticeCert partsᵛ 0F prinᵛ prinTrᵛ ∧-table ∨-table joinTrᵛ

docs.title: The verification
docs.text:
One decision for the whole certificate, one for the meet-table match; both compute to yes — that computation is the re-verification of every engine claim above.

open LatticeCheck 𝑭 𝑺

certOK : LatticeCertOK cert
certOK = from-yes (latticeCertOK? cert)

certMeet : MeetMatches 𝑭 𝑺 𝑳 cert
certMeet = from-yes (meetMatches? 𝑭 𝑺 𝑳 cert)

docs.title: The headline theorems
docs.text:
The target lattice is decidably representable, witnessed by this algebra; and the certificate's congruence list is a complete Layer-D enumeration of the algebra's decidable congruences.

SLR19-Representableᵈ : Representableᵈ (toLattice 𝑳)
SLR19-Representableᵈ = certRepresentableᵈ 𝑭 𝑺 𝑳 cert certOK certMeet

SLR19-FiniteCongruencesᵈ : FiniteCongruencesᵈ 𝑨
SLR19-FiniteCongruencesᵈ = certFiniteCongruencesᵈ cert certOK

docs.title: A machine-checked representation: Con(B21) ≅ manuscript L21
docs.text:
This is the FLRP.Certificates.SmallLatticeReps.SLR21 module of the Agda Universal Algebra Library.

This module was emitted by scripts/python/flrp/emit_agda.py from scripts/python/flrp/inputs/slr/slr21.json. Do not edit it by hand; rerun the emitter instead.

B21/L21 in the numbering of the DeMeo–Freese–Jipsen manuscript Representing Finite Lattices as Congruence Lattices of Finite Algebras (§ 6 of the 2016-06-10 draft, docs/papers/fin-lat-rep/SmallLatticeReps.tex). The dictionary between the manuscript's lattice numbering and this library's names is docs/notes/flrp-slr-naming.md.

It re-verifies, end-to-end through the WP-6 certificate pipeline (#457), the claim that the congruence lattice of the algebra "B21" — carrier size 9, unary operations f, g, h — is isomorphic to the lattice "manuscript L21" (7 elements). The engine's output below (normal-form parent vectors, Freese traces, and pointer tables) is certificate data only: the search-free checkers of Setoid.Congruences.Certificates re-verify all of it during type-checking, and the FLRP.Certificates assembly turns the checked certificate into the headline theorems — a Representableᵈ witness for the target lattice and a FiniteCongruencesᵈ instance for the algebra. Nothing is believed on the engine's authority: a wrong table or trace would make a decidable check compute to no and break compilation.

{-# OPTIONS --cubical-compatible --exact-split --safe #-}

-- Imports from Agda and the Agda Standard Library -----------------------------

                                               ; certRepresentableᵈ )

docs.title: The algebra, from its operation tables
docs.text:
Row f of opTables is the value table of the f-th unary operation; Classical.Structures.Unary turns the table into the algebra and its finiteness witnesses.

opTables : Vec (Vec (Fin 9) 9) 3
opTables = (3F ∷ 3F ∷ 4F ∷ 8F ∷ 8F ∷ 2F ∷ 2F ∷ 3F ∷ 4F ∷ [])
         ∷ (0F ∷ 0F ∷ 6F ∷ 1F ∷ 1F ∷ 0F ∷ 0F ∷ 5F ∷ 6F ∷ [])
         ∷ (4F ∷ 5F ∷ 5F ∷ 7F ∷ 8F ∷ 8F ∷ 7F ∷ 4F ∷ 4F ∷ [])
         ∷ []

𝑨 : Algebra {𝑆 = Sig-Unary (Fin 3)} 0ℓ 0ℓ
𝑨 = tablesToUnaryAlgebra 9 3 opTables

𝑭 : FiniteAlgebra 𝑨
𝑭 = tablesToUnaryAlgebra-FiniteAlgebra 9 3 opTables

𝑺 : FiniteSignature (Sig-Unary (Fin 3))
𝑺 = Sig-Unary-Fin-FiniteSignature 3

docs.title: The target lattice, from its Cayley tables
docs.text:
The claimed congruence lattice "manuscript L21", presented exactly as the worked lattice examples are (Examples.Classical.Lattices.L7): meet and join tables, every law discharged by decision over the finite carrier.

∧-table ∨-table : Table 7
∧-table = (0F ∷ 0F ∷ 0F ∷ 0F ∷ 0F ∷ 0F ∷ 0F ∷ [])
        ∷ (0F ∷ 1F ∷ 0F ∷ 0F ∷ 1F ∷ 1F ∷ 1F ∷ [])
        ∷ (0F ∷ 0F ∷ 2F ∷ 0F ∷ 0F ∷ 2F ∷ 2F ∷ [])
        ∷ (0F ∷ 0F ∷ 0F ∷ 3F ∷ 0F ∷ 0F ∷ 3F ∷ [])
        ∷ (0F ∷ 1F ∷ 0F ∷ 0F ∷ 4F ∷ 4F ∷ 4F ∷ [])
        ∷ (0F ∷ 1F ∷ 2F ∷ 0F ∷ 4F ∷ 5F ∷ 5F ∷ [])
        ∷ (0F ∷ 1F ∷ 2F ∷ 3F ∷ 4F ∷ 5F ∷ 6F ∷ [])
        ∷ []

∨-table = (0F ∷ 1F ∷ 2F ∷ 3F ∷ 4F ∷ 5F ∷ 6F ∷ [])
        ∷ (1F ∷ 1F ∷ 5F ∷ 6F ∷ 4F ∷ 5F ∷ 6F ∷ [])

open FiniteLattice

𝑳 : FiniteLattice
𝑳 .size     = 6
𝑳 ._∧_      = ⟦ ∧-table ⟧
𝑳 ._∨_      = ⟦ ∨-table ⟧

docs.title: The certificate
docs.text:
The engine's whole-lattice certificate (design note § 4): the congruence list as normal-form parent vectors, indexed by the lattice's carrier; the principal-congruence pointer table with one Freese trace per carrier pair; and the join traces, seeded by forest edges. The meet and join tables are the target's own tables, which is what MeetMatches pins.

docs.title: The verification
docs.text:
One decision for the whole certificate, one for the meet-table match; both compute to yes — that computation is the re-verification of every engine claim above.

open LatticeCheck 𝑭 𝑺

certOK : LatticeCertOK cert
certOK = from-yes (latticeCertOK? cert)

certMeet : MeetMatches 𝑭 𝑺 𝑳 cert
certMeet = from-yes (meetMatches? 𝑭 𝑺 𝑳 cert)

docs.title: The headline theorems
docs.text:
The target lattice is decidably representable, witnessed by this algebra; and the certificate's congruence list is a complete Layer-D enumeration of the algebra's decidable congruences.

SLR21-Representableᵈ : Representableᵈ (toLattice 𝑳)

docs.title: A machine-checked representation: Con(B23) ≅ manuscript L23
docs.text:
This is the FLRP.Certificates.SmallLatticeReps.SLR23 module of the Agda Universal Algebra Library.

This module was emitted by scripts/python/flrp/emit_agda.py from scripts/python/flrp/inputs/slr/slr23.json. Do not edit it by hand; rerun the emitter instead.

B23/L23 in the numbering of the DeMeo–Freese–Jipsen manuscript Representing Finite Lattices as Congruence Lattices of Finite Algebras (§ 6 of the 2016-06-10 draft, docs/papers/fin-lat-rep/SmallLatticeReps.tex). The dictionary between the manuscript's lattice numbering and this library's names is docs/notes/flrp-slr-naming.md.

It re-verifies, end-to-end through the WP-6 certificate pipeline (#457), the claim that the congruence lattice of the algebra "B23" — carrier size 6, unary operations f, g, h, k — is isomorphic to the lattice "manuscript L23" (7 elements). The engine's output below (normal-form parent vectors, Freese traces, and pointer tables) is certificate data only: the search-free checkers of Setoid.Congruences.Certificates re-verify all of it during type-checking, and the FLRP.Certificates assembly turns the checked certificate into the headline theorems — a Representableᵈ witness for the target lattice and a FiniteCongruencesᵈ instance for the algebra. Nothing is believed on the engine's authority: a wrong table or trace would make a decidable check compute to no and break compilation.

docs.title: The algebra, from its operation tables
docs.text:
Row f of opTables is the value table of the f-th unary operation; Classical.Structures.Unary turns the table into the algebra and its finiteness witnesses.

opTables : Vec (Vec (Fin 6) 6) 4
opTables = (0F ∷ 1F ∷ 0F ∷ 1F ∷ 4F ∷ 4F ∷ [])
         ∷ (1F ∷ 1F ∷ 3F ∷ 3F ∷ 4F ∷ 5F ∷ [])
         ∷ (3F ∷ 2F ∷ 3F ∷ 2F ∷ 5F ∷ 5F ∷ [])
         ∷ (4F ∷ 1F ∷ 5F ∷ 3F ∷ 4F ∷ 5F ∷ [])
         ∷ []

𝑨 : Algebra {𝑆 = Sig-Unary (Fin 4)} 0ℓ 0ℓ
𝑨 = tablesToUnaryAlgebra 6 4 opTables

𝑭 : FiniteAlgebra 𝑨
𝑭 = tablesToUnaryAlgebra-FiniteAlgebra 6 4 opTables

𝑺 : FiniteSignature (Sig-Unary (Fin 4))
𝑺 = Sig-Unary-Fin-FiniteSignature 4

docs.title: The target lattice, from its Cayley tables
docs.text:
The claimed congruence lattice "manuscript L23", presented exactly as the worked lattice examples are (Examples.Classical.Lattices.L7): meet and join tables, every law discharged by decision over the finite carrier.

∧-table ∨-table : Table 7
∧-table = (0F ∷ 0F ∷ 0F ∷ 0F ∷ 0F ∷ 0F ∷ 0F ∷ [])
        ∷ (0F ∷ 1F ∷ 0F ∷ 0F ∷ 1F ∷ 1F ∷ 1F ∷ [])
        ∷ (0F ∷ 0F ∷ 2F ∷ 0F ∷ 2F ∷ 2F ∷ 2F ∷ [])
        ∷ (0F ∷ 0F ∷ 0F ∷ 3F ∷ 0F ∷ 0F ∷ 3F ∷ [])
        ∷ (0F ∷ 1F ∷ 2F ∷ 0F ∷ 4F ∷ 4F ∷ 4F ∷ [])
        ∷ (0F ∷ 1F ∷ 2F ∷ 0F ∷ 4F ∷ 5F ∷ 5F ∷ [])
        ∷ (0F ∷ 1F ∷ 2F ∷ 3F ∷ 4F ∷ 5F ∷ 6F ∷ [])
        ∷ []

∨-table = (0F ∷ 1F ∷ 2F ∷ 3F ∷ 4F ∷ 5F ∷ 6F ∷ [])
        ∷ (1F ∷ 1F ∷ 4F ∷ 6F ∷ 4F ∷ 5F ∷ 6F ∷ [])

𝑳 : FiniteLattice
𝑳 .size     = 6
𝑳 ._∧_      = ⟦ ∧-table ⟧
𝑳 ._∨_      = ⟦ ∨-table ⟧
